'''Alexander Mihailovich Zamorzaev''' ({{langx|ru|Александр Михайлович Заморзаев}}; 27{{nbsp}}January 1927 – 1{{nbsp}}November 1997) was a Soviet mathematician and crystallographer. In 1953 Zamorzaev was the first to derive the complete list of [[magnetic space group]]s ([[Alexei Vasilievich Shubnikov|Shubnikov]] groups).<ref>Zamorzaev, A.M. (1953). ''Generalization of Fedorov groups'', Master's dissertation, Leningrad State University (in Russian)</ref><ref>Zamorzaev, A.M. (1957). ''Generalization of Fedorov groups'', Sov. Phys. Cryst., '''2''', 10-15</ref><ref>Zamorzaev, A.M. (1963). ''On the 1651 Shubnikov groups'', Sov. Phys. Cryst., '''7''', 661-668</ref> In 1957 Zamorzaev founded the field of generalised [[Dichromatic symmetry|antisymmetry]] by introducing the concept of more than one kind of two-valued antisymmetry operation ([[multiple antisymmetry]]).<ref>Zamorzaev, A.M. and Sokolov, E.I. (1957). ''Symmetry and various kinds of antisymmetry of finite bodies'', Sov. Phys. Cryst., '''2''', 5-9</ref>

==Life==

===Career===

Zamorzaev was born on 23 January 1927 in Leningrad. In 1953 at the University of Leningrad, under the supervision of [[Aleksandr Aleksandrov (mathematician)|A.D. Aleksandrov]], he gained the M.A. degree with the dissertation ''Generalization of Fedorov groups'', in which he developed the general theory of [[Dichromatic symmetry|antisymmetry]]. In this work he derived for the first time the 1651 antisymmetry space groups, and named them "Shubnikov groups", after [[Alexei Vasilievich Shubnikov|A.V. Shubnikov]] the pioneer of antisymmetry.<ref>Palistrant, A.F. and Jablan, S.V. (1997). ''[https://www.jstor.org/stable/43996983 Alexander Mihailovich Zamorzaev]'', Filomat (Nis), '''11''', 157-159</ref>

In 1953 he became a mathematics lecturer at the newly opened [[Moldova State University|University of Kishinev (Chișinău)]]. Besides teaching the regular mathematics curriculum, and supervising graduate students, Zamorzaev devised and taught new courses in the areas of [[discrete geometry]], theoretical [[crystallography]], and [[Dichromatic symmetry|antisymmetry]] and its generalisations. 

In 1971 he gained his doctoral degree with a thesis entitled ''Theory of Antisymmetry and its Different Generalizations''. The thesis was based on his new theories of geometry and mathematical crystallography, 1) multiple antisymmetry;<ref name=multiple_antisymmetry>Zamorzaev A.M. (1976). ''Theory of simple and multiple antisymmetry''. Chisinau: Stiintza, 283 p. (in Russian)</ref> 2) similarity and conformal symmetry;<ref name=similarity>Zamorzaev, A.M. (1964). ''Similarity symmetric and antisymmetric groups'', Sov. Phys. Cryst., '''8''', 553-558</ref> and 3) P-symmetry,<ref name=p-symmetry>Zamorzaev A.M., Karpova Yu.S., Lungu A.P. and Palistrant A.F. (1986). ''P-symmetry and its further development''. Chisinau: Stiintsa, 156 p. (in Russian)</ref> including generalisations of A. V. Shubnikov's antisymmetry and [[Nikolay Belov (geochemist)|N. V. Belov]]'s [[Polychromatic symmetry|color symmetry]].<ref>Palistrant, A.F. and Jablan, S.V. (2008). ''[https://www.iucr.org/news/newsletter/volume-6/number-4/a.-m.-zamorzaev-1927-1997 A. M. Zamorzaev (1927-1997)]'', IUCr Newsletter, '''6'''(4)</ref>
 
In 1973 a department of higher geometry was established within the university and Zamorzaev was appointed as professor and head of the department.<ref>Unsigned obituary (1998). ''Alexander Mihailovich Zamorzaev'', Cryst. Reports, '''43''', 530-531</ref> A history of the personnel and achievements of Zamorzaev's school of geometry is available online.<ref>Palistrant, A.F. (2002). ''[http://www.mi.sanu.ac.rs/vismath/zam/index.html Professor A. M. Zamorzaev (1927-1997) and Kishinev school of discrete geometry]'', Vismath, '''4'''(1)</ref>

===Works===

The majority of Zamorzaev's works were published in Russian. Books published by Zamorzaev:

* Theory of simple and multiple antisymmetry (1976)<ref name=multiple_antisymmetry/>
* Theory of discrete symmetry groups (1977)<ref>Zamorzaev A.M. and Palistrant A.F. (1977). ''Theory of discrete symmetry groups''. Chisinau: Izd-vo KSU, 101 p. (in Russian)</ref>
* Color symmetry, its generalizations and applications (1978)<ref>Zamorzaev A.M., Galyarsky E.I. and Palistrant A.F. (1978). ''Color symmetry, its generalizations and applications''. Chisinau: Styintsa, 275 p. (in Russian)</ref>
* P-symmetry and its further development (1986)<ref>Zamorzaev A.M., Karpova Yu.S., Lungu A.P. and Palistrant A.F. (1986). ''P-symmetry and its further development''. Chisinau: Stiintsa, 156 p. (in Russian)</ref>

Zamorzaev published 110 papers. Selected papers available in English:

* Similarity symmetric and antisymmetric groups (1964).<ref name=similarity/>
* Quasisymmetry (p-symmetry) groups (1968)<ref name=p-symmetry/>
* Color-symmetry space groups (1969)<ref>Zamorzaev, A.M. (1969). ''Color-symmetry space groups'', Sov. Phys. Cryst., '''14''', 155-159</ref>
* Antisymmetry, its generalizations and geometrical applications (1980)<ref>Zamorzaev, A.M. and Palistrant, A.F. (1980). ''Antisymmetry, its generalizations and geometrical applications'', Z. Krist., '''151''', 231-248, {{doi|10.1524/zkri.1980.151.3-4.231}}</ref>
* Generalized antisymmetry (1988).<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Zamorzaev|first1=A.M.|year=1988|url=https://core.ac.uk/download/pdf/82277227.pdf|title=Generalized antisymmetry|journal=Comput. Math. Applic.|volume=16|issue=5–8|pages=555–562|doi=10.1016/0898-1221(88)90245-3|doi-access=free}}</ref>

===Honours and awards===

* [[E. S. Fedorov]] Prize of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] for his contributions to the theory of [[symmetry]] (1973)
* State Prize of the [[Moldavian Soviet Socialist Republic|Moldovan SSR]] in Science and Technology for his contributions in the field of [[discrete geometry]] (1974)
* Honored Worker of Science of the Moldovan SSR for his achievements in science and education (1977)
* Elected Corresponding Member of the [[Academy of Sciences of Moldova]] (1989)
